subject: ARTS
disclaimer: NU Map is an independent, student-built planner. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to Northeastern University. Data is scraped from Northeastern's public catalog and refreshed on a schedule; always confirm with the official catalog and an academic advisor.

legend.prereqs: Flat token list: course refs {subject, number, minGrade} joined by 'And'/'Or' strings; nested arrays are parenthesized groups. minGrade is the minimum passing grade required.
legend.coreqs: Courses that must be taken in the same term.
legend.offerings.terms: Past/scheduled terms by Banner code (YYYY = academic-year END year; Fall runs in YYYY-1). sections/enrolled/capacity are snapshots from the scheduled scrape, NOT live seat availability.
legend.offerings.typicalDays: Weekdays on which at least 50% of recent sections met.
legend.offerings.daysPct: Percent of recent sections meeting on each weekday (M/T/W/Th/F).
legend.offerings.meetingPatterns: [pattern, percent-of-sections] pairs; in patterns like 'MWR', R means Thursday.
legend.instructors: Per season. sharePct = average percent of that season's enrolled students taught by this professor (recent terms). 'reviews' links their RateMyHusky page when one exists.
legend.level: undergrad for course numbers below 5000, grad otherwise.
legend.typicallyOffered: Seasons in which the course was scheduled in at least two-thirds of that season's terms on record since it first appeared — a pattern, not a guarantee.
legend.unlocks: Courses that list this course in their prerequisites — what taking it opens up.
legend.nuPath: NUpath general-education attributes this course carries.
legend.repeatable: Whether the course may be taken more than once for credit (repeatMax / repeatMaxSH cap it).

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Painting Basics
courses.description: Presents an introductory studio course in the fundamental techniques of painting. Formal problems in the study of color, light, space systems, form, and composition establish the foundation for more individual creative expression. Uses critiques and slide lectures as needed.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Figure Drawing
courses.description: Focuses on developing the student’s awareness of the structure of the figure as well as the emotive qualities of “figuration.” Students draw from a model in each class. They also develop drawings based on the political and social concerns of contemporary culture and the role of gender as seen through “image.”

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Topics in Studio Arts
courses.description: Explores studio arts topics, supporting work in all studio arts disciplines. Examines current discourse in the field and draws on instructor expertise. Students develop original creative projects in response to the topic, informed by critical readings, instructor and guest lectures, examination of other artists' works, and class discussions. Emphasizes skill development and strategies for self-directed studio arts production including experimentation, planning, iteration, revision, and critique of creative work. May be repeated up to five times.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Drawing in Mixed Media
courses.description: Offers an upper-level course designed for students who want to explore the ever-changing discipline of drawing, which has now become a medium that stands on its own. Explores a range of media for generating drawings, including traditional techniques and computer-based media. Emphasizes open-ended application and interpretation of drawing as a medium. Requires students to attend lectures and exhibitions and keep a journal.

courses.subject: ARTS
courses.title: Drawing from Object to Concept
courses.description: Covers the practice of drawing as a fundamental mode of communication and tool for ideation. Teaches drawing through observation of real-world objects and conceptualization of abstract ideas related to personal interests. Develops practical skills to construct two-dimensional images, become familiar with a range of traditional drawing materials, and integrate digital techniques. Focuses on process, perception, critical dialogue, and self-directed research.
